hallelujah-chorus.sources: // Sources: the song file (the parts' guide notes, as built 2026-11-18), tools: ~/Code/arranger-keep/partfacts.py; licence.source: Handel, Messiah, ed. Ebenezer Prout (London: Novello, 1902), full score, No. 44, Handel's own four voice parts, sung in B-flat (printed in D)

parts.soprano: Sings the top line, most often on B-flat, then F and C, up to its top F only once, on "He" as the sopranos first come in with "and He shall reign", and down to its low B-flat on "Om-" in the first "Lord God Omnipotent", on "world" and "come" (and the notes sliding down into them) in "The kingdom of this world is become", and on "for ever," in the sopranos' second "He shall reign for ever and ever".
parts.alto: Sings the alto line, most often on F, then B-flat and D, up to its top B-flat only on "He" as the altos come in with "and He shall reign", both times, and down to its low F only on the "eth" of the first "reigneth" and on a "jah," in the Hallelujahs under the tenors' and basses' "for the Lord God".
parts.tenor: Sings the tenor line, most often on B-flat, then F and D, up to its top F only on the "lu" of the Hallelujah just before the tenors' "for the Lord God Omnipotent" and on "He" as the tenors come in with "and He shall reign", and down to its low B-flat only on "Om-" of "Omnipotent" (twice), on the "eth" of the "reigneth" the altos, tenors and basses sing together, and on the "dom" of "The kingdom of this world".
parts.bass: Sings the bass line, most often on B-flat, then F and D, up to its top B-flat often (51 notes), among them the "lu" of many Hallelujahs, "God" in "Lord God Omnipotent", "the" in "the Kingdom of our Lord", "He" as the basses begin "and He shall reign", and "Kings," and "Lords," near the end, and down to its low E-flat only once, on "Om-" when the altos, tenors and basses sing "for the Lord God Omnipotent" together.

parts_es.soprano: Canta la línea más aguda, con más frecuencia en el Si bemol, luego en el Fa y el Do, sube a su Fa agudo solo una vez, en "He" cuando las sopranos entran por primera vez con "and He shall reign", y baja a su Si bemol grave en "Om-" del primer "Lord God Omnipotent", en "world" y "come" (y en las notas que bajan hasta ellas) de "The kingdom of this world is become", y en "for ever," del segundo "He shall reign for ever and ever" de las sopranos.
parts_es.alto: Canta la línea de contralto, con más frecuencia en el Fa, luego en el Si bemol y el Re, sube a su Si bemol agudo solo en "He" cuando las contraltos entran con "and He shall reign", las dos veces, y baja a su Fa grave solo en el "eth" del primer "reigneth" y en un "jah," de los Hallelujahs bajo el "for the Lord God" de los tenores y los bajos.
parts_es.tenor: Canta la línea de tenor, con más frecuencia en el Si bemol, luego en el Fa y el Re, sube a su Fa agudo solo en el "lu" del Hallelujah justo antes del "for the Lord God Omnipotent" de los tenores y en "He" cuando los tenores entran con "and He shall reign", y baja a su Si bemol grave solo en "Om-" de "Omnipotent" (dos veces), en el "eth" del "reigneth" que cantan juntos contraltos, tenores y bajos, y en el "dom" de "The kingdom of this world".
parts_es.bass: Canta la línea del bajo, con más frecuencia en el Si bemol, luego en el Fa y el Re, sube a su Si bemol agudo a menudo (51 notas), entre ellas el "lu" de muchos Hallelujahs, "God" en "Lord God Omnipotent", "the" en "the Kingdom of our Lord", "He" cuando los bajos empiezan "and He shall reign", y "Kings," y "Lords," cerca del final, y baja a su Mi bemol grave solo una vez, en "Om-" cuando contraltos, tenores y bajos cantan juntos "for the Lord God Omnipotent".
